Rashi on Arakhin 10b:10:1.english: Because its sound is sweet [ḥali] - its sound is sweet to hear:

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:11:2.english: Thin - [in Old French:] tinbesh. [That is,] its walls [giluddo] were thin:

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:11:3.hebrew: צלצל - שני כלים מכין זה ע"ג זה, וקולם דק, וקורין להן בלע"ז צנב"ש:
Rashi on Arakhin 10b:11:3.english: A cymbal - [It consists of] two vessels that one strikes one on top of the other, and their sound is high-pitched, and they call them [in Old French] "tzanbash":

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:12:1.hebrew: מפטמת את הבשמים - שבה היו כותשין סממני הקטרת, והיה קולה צלול, ומפטמת הבשמים יפה ונותנת בהן ריח, כדאמרי' בכריתות (דף ו:): השוחק אומר "היטב הדק, הדק היטב", שהקול יפה לבשמים:
Rashi on Arakhin 10b:12:1.english: Compounded the spices - For in it they would pound the ingredients of the incense, and its sound was clear, and it compounded the spices well and imparted fragrance to them, as we say in Keritot (6b): The one who grinds says, "Grind well, grind fine; grind fine, grind well," because the sound is good for the spices:

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:13:1.english: Two vessels - the cymbal and the copper mortar:

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:13:2.english: Burnished - Thin, such that one can fold it:

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:15:1.english: Pairs - two cymbals and two mortars:

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:16:1.english: About the size of an issar - The mouth of the spring from which it flows was as wide as an issar.

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:16:2.hebrew: אל יתהלל חכם - שחכמתו אינה אלא מקלקלת, לפי שכלי מקדש ראשון ע"פ הגבורה נעשו, דכתיב (ד"ה א כח): הכל בכתב מיד ה' עלי השכיל כל מלאכת התבנית:
Rashi on Arakhin 10b:16:2.english: Let not the wise man glory - For his wisdom only spoils [it], because the vessels of the First Temple were made by the word of the Almighty, as it is written (I Chronicles 28:19): "All in writing from the hand of the Lord upon me He made me understand, all the works of the pattern."

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:17:1.hebrew: הרדווליס טבלא גורגדנא - זוג ועינבל, שקורים אישקליט"א:
Rashi on Arakhin 10b:17:1.english: Hirdavlis, tabla gurgdana - A bell and clapper, which they call eschelette.

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:17:2.english: And disrupts the melody - When this sound would conclude.

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:18:1.hebrew: מגריפה - שבה גורפין את דשן המזבח, וודי"ל, והוא כעין כף:
Rashi on Arakhin 10b:18:1.english: Magreifa - [That] with which they shovel the ash of the altar; vadil, and it is like a scoop.

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:1:1.hebrew: ימי החג חלוקין בקרבנותיהם - דפרי החג מתמעטין והולכין:
Rashi on Arakhin 10b:1:1.english: The days of the festival [of Sukkot] are distinct from one another in their offerings - For the bulls of the festival decrease progressively [each day]:

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:3:1.hebrew: ראש חדש איקרי מועד - דכתיב (איכה א׳:ט״ו): "קרא עלי מועד". ובפ"ד דמסכת תענית (דף כט.): תמוז דההוא שתא מלויי מליוה, דכתיב "קרא עלי מועד":
Rashi on Arakhin 10b:3:1.english: The New Moon is called an appointed day - as it is written (Lamentations 1:15): "He has proclaimed against me an appointed time." And in the fourth chapter of tractate Taanit (page 29a): [the month of] Tammuz of that year was intercalated [with an extra day], as it is written: "He has proclaimed against me an appointed time":

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:3:3.english: Sanctified - [as a Festival] with regard to the performance of labor:

Rashi on Arakhin 10b:8:1.english: Its reading - the reading of the Megilla:

Tosafot on Arakhin 10b:12:1.hebrew: ועליהם אמר דוד נחושת ממורט - פ"ה על נחושת שמוציא בהם. מיהו קשה, דהאי קרא בעלמא במלכים דכתיב "נחשת ממורט", ובדברי הימים (ב ד) כתיב "נחשת מרוק", ומאי קאמר "ועליהם אמר דוד"? ונראה לר"י דה"ג: ועליהם אמר קרא "נחשת ממורט" נחושת (ממורק):
Tosafot on Arakhin 10b:12:1.english: And about them David said: "Polished copper" - Rashi explains [this as referring] to the copper that [the mortar] gives off through them. However, it is difficult, for this verse appears only in [the book of] Kings, where it is written "polished [mimorat] copper," whereas in Chronicles (II 4) it is written "burnished [maruk] copper." And what does [the Gemara] mean by "And about them David said"? It seems to Rabbi Yitzchak that this is the correct reading: And about them the verse said: "Polished copper" — copper [that is] burnished:

Tosafot on Arakhin 10b:17:1.hebrew: הרדווליס - בסמ"ך גריס רש"י, ונראה לר' הרדוולים במ"ם. וכן יש בבראשית רבה: "ערדולין בעיר ומדינה נהפכה". פירוש: ערדוולין כמו הרדוולין, והם מיני כלי זמר; מ"ם מתחלפת בנו"ן. הרדוולים — זהו תרגום של עוגב:
Tosafot on Arakhin 10b:17:1.english: Hirdavlis - Rashi reads [the text] with a samekh, and it appears to the Rabbi [to read] hirdavlim with a mem. And so it is in Bereishit Rabbah: "An ardulin is in the city, and the province is overturned." Explanation: ardavlin is like hardavlin, and they are types of musical instruments; [and a final] mem interchanges with [a final] nun. Hirdavlim — this is the translation of "ugav" [in the Targum].

Tosafot on Arakhin 10b:18:1.hebrew: מגריפה היתה במקדש - פי' בקונטרס שגורפין בה הדשן. וקשה, דהא היתה כלי זמר! אלא נראה לפרש, דשני מיני מגריפות היו: אחת לדשן, ואחת של שיר:
Tosafot on Arakhin 10b:18:1.english: "There was a magreifa in the Temple" - [Rashi] explains in the Kuntres that they would shovel the ashes with it. And this is difficult, for behold, it was a musical instrument! Rather, it appears [correct] to explain that there were two types of magreifot: one for the ashes, and one for song.

Tosafot on Arakhin 10b:5:1.hebrew: אמרו מלאכי השרת מפני מה אין ישראל אומרים שירה לפניך בר"ה וביום הכיפורים - אבל לא קאמר "מפני מה אין אנו אומרים שירה", משמע שמלאכי השרת אומרים שירה. ולכך אומר ר"י דבר"ה וביום הכיפורים אין לדלג, "והחיות ישוררו וכרובים יפארו":
Tosafot on Arakhin 10b:5:1.english: The ministering angels said: For what reason do the Jewish people not recite songs of praise before You on Rosh HaShana and on Yom Kippur - But [the angels] did not say, "For what reason do we not recite song?" This implies that the ministering angels do recite song. And therefore Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that on Rosh HaShana and on Yom Kippur one should not skip [the recitation of the Kedushah liturgy], [for] "the Ḥayyot shall sing and the Cherubim shall give praise":
